# Rule sets

A rule set picks the catalogue rules a machine assumes (`use`), sets their parameters (`param`), may `include` another set, `drop` rules, or write its own. The rules marked core (R0, R1, R8, R24) hold in every set. `python -m qccd.ruleset show <set>` prints any set resolved.

## A leaderboard entry's own rule set (rules.json)

- A bundle may carry `rules.json` (kind `qccd.rules`, version 1): a shipped set by name, or a set written for the design. The grader judges the entry by it, and still checks the board's set: the report's `conformance` says which board rules the entry breaks, drops, replaces or adds.
- Read only by `qccd.ruleset.declared.load_declared`: at most 64 KB and 200 rules; level `device`; `include` may name only a shipped set; the core rules must be exactly the catalogue's.
- Rankings list only entries that keep every board rule with the board's physics; `?rules=all` lists the others, tagged.

<a id="set-c2lr"></a>
### `c2lr`: C2LR swap-or-stay

This website's machine on a C2LR lattice: every rule of the standard set, and C1-C10. A swap-or-stay step's routes are the device's matching, so the junction, rail, passing and one-waveform rules (R2, R3, R5, R22) do not judge its crossings; R4 still asks for its class. Both pairings are allowed: one diagonal at every junction (demonstrated) and the two-pair checkerboard steps (assumed, and marked so in every report).

- include: `"standard"`
- Rules (41): C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8 C9 C10 R0 R1 R2 R3 R4 R4b R4d R5 R6 R6b R7 R7b R7c R8 R9 R10 R11 R12 R13 R14 R15 R16 R17 R18 R19 R20 R21 R22 R23 R24 R25
- param `max_chain = 15`: the most ions a gate's chain may hold (R13)
- param `c2lr_forms = {"diagonal", "checkerboard"}`: how a C2LR step may pair legs (C6): "diagonal", one diagonal at every junction (demonstrated), and "checkerboard", two pairs at the junctions of one colour (assumed)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-c2lr

<a id="set-c2lr-demonstrated"></a>
### `c2lr-demonstrated`: C2LR swap-or-stay, as demonstrated

The C2LR rule set with only what arXiv:2403.00756 demonstrated: every junction runs the same single diagonal (W-S, W-N, E-S or E-N). A step that pairs two diagonals at the junctions of one checkerboard colour breaks C6.

- include: `"c2lr"`
- Rules (41): C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8 C9 C10 R0 R1 R2 R3 R4 R4b R4d R5 R6 R6b R7 R7b R7c R8 R9 R10 R11 R12 R13 R14 R15 R16 R17 R18 R19 R20 R21 R22 R23 R24 R25
- param `max_chain = 15`: the most ions a gate's chain may hold (R13)
- param `c2lr_forms = {"diagonal"}`: how a C2LR step may pair legs (C6): "diagonal", one diagonal at every junction (demonstrated), and "checkerboard", two pairs at the junctions of one colour (assumed)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-c2lr-demonstrated

<a id="set-cyclone"></a>
### `cyclone`: Cyclone's rules

A trap does one gate, split or merge at a time; a rail and a junction hold one ion at a time; the compiler keeps a list of ions per trap, not a chain, so no chain order is tracked; every operation lasts what Cyclone's duration law says; each qubit's gates run in the circuit's order, except that consecutive CNOTs in which it plays the same role may run in any order.

- Rules (10): R0 R1 R2 R3 R6b R8 R24 R26 R27 R29
- param `serial_kinds = {"gate2", "split", "merge"}`: the operation kinds that hold their trap one at a time (R27), named as kind(o) names them
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-cyclone

<a id="set-ionshuttler"></a>
### `ionshuttler`: IonShuttler's rules (exact router)

A rail and a junction hold one ion at a time; every operation lasts one time step of the paper's model; each qubit's gates run in the circuit's order. The paper's replay also checks its own model's rules about the processing zone, beside these.

- Rules (8): R0 R1 R2 R3 R8 R24 R25 R29
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-ionshuttler

<a id="set-ionshuttler-heuristic"></a>
### `ionshuttler-heuristic`: IonShuttler's rules (heuristic router)

As the exact router's rules, except that the heuristic lets two chains pass the processing zone in one step, so rails and junctions are not held to one ion at a time here; the paper's replay checks its own rules about that zone instead.

- Rules (6): R0 R1 R8 R24 R25 R29
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-ionshuttler-heuristic

<a id="set-jones"></a>
### `jones`: Surface-code QCCD's rules

A trap does one operation of any kind at a time; a rail and a junction hold one ion at a time; a reorder before a split is a gate swap; operations that the schedule says hold the same component never overlap; every operation lasts what the paper's duration law says; each qubit's gates run in the circuit's order, except that consecutive CNOTs in which it plays the same role may run in any order.

- Rules (12): R0 R1 R2 R3 R6b R8 R14 R24 R26 R27 R29 R30
- param `serial_kinds = {"gate2", "gate1", "split", "merge", "swap", "measure", "reset"}`: the operation kinds that hold their trap one at a time (R27), named as kind(o) names them
- param `chain_order = "physical"`: how the order inside a chain is followed through a reorder before a split: "qccdsim" lifts the departing ion out where it stood, "physical" moves the end ion's state into its place (read by R14)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-jones

<a id="set-qccdsim"></a>
### `qccdsim`: QCCDSim's rules

The rules QCCDSim's scheduler enforces: a trap does one gate, split or merge at a time; a shuttle reserves its whole path, so a rail and a junction hold one ion at a time; a split takes the end ion of its chain or pays for a reorder (the reordered ion is lifted out where it stood); every operation lasts what QCCDSim's duration law says; each qubit's gates run in the circuit's order.

- Rules (11): R0 R1 R2 R3 R6b R8 R14 R24 R25 R27 R29
- param `serial_kinds = {"gate2", "split", "merge"}`: the operation kinds that hold their trap one at a time (R27), named as kind(o) names them
- param `chain_order = "qccdsim"`: how the order inside a chain is followed through a reorder before a split: "qccdsim" lifts the departing ion out where it stood, "physical" moves the end ion's state into its place (read by R14)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-qccdsim

<a id="set-qccdsim-gateset"></a>
### `qccdsim-gateset`: QCCDSim's rules, with the circuit's gates as a set

QCCDSim's rules for benchmark files that list a round's CNOTs with no order between stabilisers: every gate must be performed, in any order.

- include: `"qccdsim"`
- drop: `R25`
- Rules (10): R0 R1 R2 R3 R6b R8 R14 R24 R27 R29
- param `serial_kinds = {"gate2", "split", "merge"}`: the operation kinds that hold their trap one at a time (R27), named as kind(o) names them
- param `chain_order = "qccdsim"`: how the order inside a chain is followed through a reorder before a split: "qccdsim" lifts the departing ion out where it stood, "physical" moves the end ion's state into its place (read by R14)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-qccdsim-gateset

<a id="set-qccdsim-physical"></a>
### `qccdsim-physical`: QCCDSim's rules, with a physical gate swap

QCCDSim's rules, except that a reorder before a split is a real gate swap: the end ion's state moves to where the departing ion stood, instead of the departing ion being lifted out in place.

- include: `"qccdsim"`
- Rules (11): R0 R1 R2 R3 R6b R8 R14 R24 R25 R27 R29
- param `serial_kinds = {"gate2", "split", "merge"}`: the operation kinds that hold their trap one at a time (R27), named as kind(o) names them
- param `chain_order = "physical"`: how the order inside a chain is followed through a reorder before a split: "qccdsim" lifts the departing ion out where it stood, "physical" moves the end ion's state into its place (read by R14)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-qccdsim-physical

<a id="set-standard"></a>
### `standard`: This website's machine

Broadcast-controlled surface traps, as the compiler and the studio model them: every rule of the catalogue that is about a programme, a device drawing or the compiler's own claims.

- Rules (31): R0 R1 R2 R3 R4 R4b R4d R5 R6 R6b R7 R7b R7c R8 R9 R10 R11 R12 R13 R14 R15 R16 R17 R18 R19 R20 R21 R22 R23 R24 R25
- param `max_chain = 15`: the most ions a gate's chain may hold (R13)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-standard

<a id="set-tiscc"></a>
### `tiscc`: TISCC's rules

One ion per zone, so a zone does not serialise its own operations; a junction is crossed by one ion at a time; rotations, preparation and measurement run only in operation (O) zones; the two-ion gate acts on ions in neighbouring zones of one rail; every gate of the circuit is performed, in any order; every operation lasts what TISCC's duration law says.

- Rules (8): R0 R1 R2 R8 R24 R29 R32 R33
- param `single_ion_zones = {"O"}`: the zones single-ion operations may run in (R32)
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-tiscc

<a id="set-trapsimd"></a>
### `trapsimd`: TrapSIMD's rules

Transport between traps is broadcast: every such move of a cycle starts and ends together and is one class of move, and cycles never overlap; one ion per position, so no chain order is tracked; a junction holds one ion at a time; the two-ion gate acts on ions in a gate zone and a neighbouring one; every operation lasts what the paper's timing table says; each qubit's gates run in the circuit's order, except that consecutive CNOTs in which it plays the same role may run in any order. The paper's replay also checks its own model's control limits (which shifts and swaps a cycle may combine), beside these.

- Rules (9): R0 R1 R2 R8 R24 R26 R29 R31 R33
- Website: https://qccd.academy/rules/#set-trapsimd
